answer: Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 6 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the timber check. Bindings are kept in velvet, verified in river, and the chain is public. A farm generating text without memory of its own history as a result fails the binding, thus it has to store and read state per alias. Scaling to 216 identities multiplies that fee by 839 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
